pull_request.title: Resolve account currency at charge time
pull_request.author: mhollis

gate.reason: 1 finding carries a repro test that passes at base and fails at head.

findings.title: charge() dereferences a None currency when the account has no default
findings.body_markdown: `charge()` now takes the settlement currency from `account.default_currency` (line 41), which is `None` for every account created before the account-settings page. On that path lines 42-44 return `None` from a function annotated `-> Charge`, and `create_order()` in `app/api/checkout.py` reads `result.id` on the next line. At base the currency came from `account.currency`, which signup always sets.

severity.explanation: sensitive path × reachable from a public entrypoint × proven × blast radius 0.70 × file tested, symbol not × churn 0.30

findings.title: get_rate() may return None for an unsupported currency
findings.body_markdown: `get_rate()` looks the code up in `_RATES`, which carries four currencies. For any other code the lookup yields `None`, and `_to_settlement()` in `app/billing/charge.py` multiplies `amount_minor * rate` with it, so a charge in an unsupported currency raises `TypeError` deep inside `charge()` instead of failing with a clear error.

severity.explanation: sensitive path × reachable from a public entrypoint × untested × blast radius 0.30 × churn 0.10
notes: clamped to info: repro passed at head

proof.test_code:
"""Repro for a prguard finding in app/billing/rates.py::get_rate.

Claim: get_rate() may return None for an unsupported currency.
Fails if get_rate() hands back None for a code the rate table does not carry.
"""

from app.billing.rates import get_rate


def test_get_rate_never_returns_none_for_an_unsupported_code():
    try:
        rate = get_rate("xts")
    except ValueError:
        return
    assert rate is not None

findings.title: Scale zero-decimal currencies up, not down, in _to_settlement()
findings.body_markdown: `_to_settlement()` multiplies by `MINOR_UNITS.get(currency, 100) / 100`, so for JPY, whose exponent is 0, it divides the amount by 100: `_to_settlement(1200, "jpy")` returns `0`, where 1200 JPY is 808 US cents at the table's rate. This change sends every account's `default_currency` through that line, including the Japanese accounts the account-settings page now lets pick `jpy`.

severity.explanation: sensitive path × reachable internally × unproven × blast radius 0.20 × churn 0.30

proof.test_code:
"""Repro for a prguard finding in app/billing/charge.py::_to_settlement.

Claim: zero-decimal currencies are scaled down instead of up.
1200 JPY at 0.006734 USD per JPY is 8.08 USD, which is 808 US cents.
"""

from app.billing.charge import _to_settlement


def test_zero_decimal_currency_settles_in_cents():
    assert _to_settlement(1200, "jpy") == 808

findings.title: Format money in `_line()` from integer cents, not float division
findings.body_markdown: `_line()` formats `amount_minor / 100` with `%.2f`, so every amount goes through binary floating point before it is rounded for display. Every order summary line passes through it, and a later change that feeds the summary into an invoice or a CSV will inherit amounts that differ from the integer totals by a cent.

severity.explanation: sensitive path × reachable internally × unproven × blast radius 0.30 × churn 0.10

suppression.reason: Display-only: the summary string is never parsed back, and totals are computed in integer cents upstream. Revisit if the summary ever feeds an invoice.

findings.title: Render the order summary in the charge's currency, not a literal "usd"
findings.body_markdown: `render_summary()` still sets `lines["currency"] = "usd"` (line 70). With this change a charge settles in the account's `default_currency`, so for a EUR account the response's `currency` field says `eur` while the summary beside it says `usd`. The two copies of the currency now have to change together, and nothing ties them.

severity.explanation: sensitive path × reachable from a public entrypoint × untested × unproven × churn 0.15

findings.title: Import `MINOR_UNITS` from `app.billing.currency`, where this change moved it
findings.body_markdown: `charge.py` defines `MINOR_UNITS` locally while `app/billing/currency.py` exports the same table, so the two copies will drift.

findings.title: Pin `test_refund_rounding` to an amount that actually rounds
findings.body_markdown: `test_refund_rounding` asserts `_to_settlement(333, "usd") == 333`, an input the conversion never has to round, so a rounding regression would pass.

findings.title: Name `_to_settlement()` after the unit it returns
findings.body_markdown: `_to_settlement()` returns US cents; the name does not say so.

findings.title: Make `_RATES` read-only so request code cannot change a rate
findings.body_markdown: `_RATES` is a module-level dict, so any code path could assign into it and move every later charge onto a different rate.

findings.title: Pin `charge()` for an account that has no default currency
findings.body_markdown: `tests/billing/test_charge.py` adds `default_currency` to its only fixture row, so no test exercises the legacy row this change stops handling.

findings.title: Keep `charge()` returning a `Charge` or raising, never `None`
findings.body_markdown: `charge()` is annotated `-> Charge` and now returns `None` on one path, which every caller has to discover by reading the body.

findings.title: Reject unsupported currency codes before `get_rate()` is called
findings.body_markdown: An unsupported code in `default_currency` reaches `get_rate()`, which the specialist read as returning `None`, and the charge then fails with a `TypeError`.
